questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
While travelling to a hilly region, you notice a massive boulder, which was loosened by heavy rains and moved downhill. This has resulted due to which of the following processes?
1. Mass wasting
2. Erosion
3. Weathering
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Mass wasting is the movement of rock and soil down slope under the influence of gravity. Rock falls, slumps, and debris flows are all examples of mass wasting. Often lubricated by rainfall or agitated by seismic activity, these events may occur very rapidly and move as a flow.
Erosion is the geological process in which earthen materials are worn away and transported by natural forces such as wind or water. A similar process, weathering, breaks down or dissolves rock, but does not involve movement. Weathering is the breaking down or dissolving of rocks and minerals on Earths surface. Once a rock has been broken down, a process called erosion transports the bits of rock and minerals away. Water, acids, salt, plants, animals, and changes in temperature are all agents of weathering and erosion.

1. These occur only on gentle slopes during rain.
2. They generally occur in clay-rich soil.
3. Earthquakes trigger landslides.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution: A landslide is defined as the movement of a mass of rock, debris, or earth down a slope. Landslides are a type of "mass wasting," which denotes any down-slope movement of soil and rock under the direct influence of gravity. Slope movement occurs when forces acting down-slope (mainly due to gravity) exceed the strength of the earth materials that compose the slope. Causes include factors that increase the effects of down-slope forces and factors that contribute to low or reduced strength. Landslides can be initiated in slopes already on the verge of movement by rainfall, snowmelt, changes in water level, stream erosion, changes in ground water, earthquakes, volcanic activity, disturbance by human activities, or any combination of these factors. Earthquake shaking and other factors can also induce landslides underwater. These landslides are called submarine landslides. Submarine landslides sometimes cause tsunamis that damage coastal areas.

questions.solution: Rain, Snow sleet or hails are the different forms of precipitation. The rain that falls from clouds but freezes before it reaches the ground is called sleet or ice pellets. Snow is precipitation that falls in the form of ice crystals. 2. Transformation of rocks is caused by weathering, erosion and metamorphic action.

questions.solution: The three processes that change one rock to another are crystallization, metamorphism, and erosion and sedimentation. Any rock can transform into any other rock by passing through one or more of these processes. This creates the rock cycle. The rock cycle is a process in which rocks are continuously transformed between the three rock types igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.

questions.solution: In geology, denudation is the long-term sum of processes that cause the wearing away of the Earth's surface by moving water, ice, wind and waves, leading to a reduction in elevation and relief of landforms and landscapes. Denudation is the wearing away of landmass by various processes like weathering, mass movement, erosion and transportation. It results in lowering the level of land, rounding exposed rock surfaces and levelling the peaks. Various agents of erosion like water, wind, and glaciers are involved in the process of denudation.

2. $A C=B C$
3. $C(A+B)=C A+C B$

questions.solution:
$C A=\left[\begin{array}{c}m \\ -m\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}m & n\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}m^2 & m n \\ -m^2 & -m n\end{array}\right]C B=\left[\begin{array}{c}m \\ -m\end{array}\right][-n-m]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-m n & -m^2 \\ m n & m^2\end{array}\right]\therefore \quad C A \neq C B$
So, statement 1 is not correct.
$\begin{aligned} & A C=\left[\begin{array}{ll}m & n\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}m \\ -m\end{array}\right]=\left[m^2-m n\right] \\ & B C=\left[\begin{array}{ll}-n & -m\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}m \\ -m\end{array}\right]=\left[-m n+m^2\right]\end{aligned}\therefore \quad A C=B C$
So, statement 2 is correct.
$\begin{aligned} & C(A+B)=\left[\begin{array}{c}m \\ -m\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}m-n & n-m\end{array}\right] \\ & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}m^2-m n & m n-m^2 \\ -m^2+m n & -m n+m^2\end{array}\right] \\ & C A+C B=\left[\begin{array}{cc}m^2-m n & m n-m^2 \\ -m^2+m n & -m n+m^2\end{array}\right]=C(A+B)\end{aligned}$
So, statement 3 is correct.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos ^4 \frac{7 \pi}{8}+\cos ^4 \frac{5 \pi}{8}=\left(\cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8}\right)^2+\left(\cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)^2 \\ = & \left(\cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8}-\cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)^2+2 \cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8} \cdot \cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8} \\ = & {\left[(-1) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{8}+\frac{5 \pi}{8}\right) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{8}-\frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos \frac{7 \pi}{8} \cdot \cos \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right]^2 } \\ = & {\left[\sin \frac{3 \pi}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos \frac{3 \pi}{2}+\cos \frac{\pi}{4}\right]^2 }\end{aligned}=\left[(-1) \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]^2=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)-\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)-\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right) \\ & =\sin \left[\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right] \sin \left[\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta-\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right]\end{aligned}\left[\because \quad \sin ^2 x-\sin ^2 y=\sin (x+y) \cdot \sin (x-y)\right]=\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \cdot \sin 2 \theta=\sin 2 \theta$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta$, where then which of the following is one of the values of $(\alpha+\beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta \\ & \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \Rightarrow & \alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $(1+\tan \theta)(1+\tan 9 \theta)=2$, then what is the value of $\tan (10 \theta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because(1+\tan \theta)(1+\tan 9 \theta)=2 \\ \Rightarrow & 1+\tan 9 \theta+\tan \theta+\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta=2 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan \theta+\tan 9 \theta=1-\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\tan \theta+\tan 9 \theta}{1-\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta}=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan (\theta+9 \theta)=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan 10 \theta=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 20^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}+\ldots .+\sin 360^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 20^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}+\ldots .+\sin 360^{\circ} \\ & =\left(\sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 360^{\circ}\right)+\left(\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 350^{\circ}\right)+\left(\sin 20^{\circ}+\right. \\ & \left.\sin 340^{\circ}\right)+\ldots+\sin 180^{\circ} \\ & =2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 180^{\circ}+2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 170^{\circ}+ \\ & \left.2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 160^{\circ}\right)+\ldots+\sin 180^{\circ} \\ & =0+0+0 \ldots .+0 \quad\left[\because \sin 180^{\circ}=0\right] \\ & =0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{\tan x+\cot x}$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$ ?
questions.solution: $f(x)=\frac{1}{\tan x+\cot x}=\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 \mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\cos 2 \mathrm{x}=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-2 \sin 2 \mathrm{x}=-2 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}=-2 \lt 0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \text { is maximum at } \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \therefore \text { Maximum value is } \\ & \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ and $2 \tan \alpha=1$, then what is $\tan 2 \beta$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \because \quad 2 \tan \alpha=1 \quad \Rightarrow 2 \tan \alpha=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=1\Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{2}+\tan \beta=1-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \tan \beta \\ \Rightarrow & 1+2 \tan \beta=2-\tan \beta \\ & \tan \beta=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$
Now, $\tan 2 \beta=\frac{2 \tan \beta}{1-\tan ^2 \beta}=\frac{2 \times \frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{9}}=\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{8}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is value of $\cot ^2 15^{\circ}+\tan ^2 15^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cot ^2 15^{\circ}+\tan ^2 15^{\circ} \\ & =\operatorname{cosec}^2 15^{\circ}-1+\sec ^2 15^{\circ}-1 \\ & =\operatorname{cosec}^2 15^{\circ}+\sec ^2 15^{\circ}-2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\sin ^2 15^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\cos ^2 15^{\circ}}-2 \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 15^{\circ}+\cos ^2 15^{\circ}}{\frac{1}{4}\left(4 \sin ^2 15^{\circ} \cdot \cos ^2 15^{\circ}\right)}-2 \\ & =\frac{4}{\sin ^2 30^{\circ}}-2=\frac{4}{\frac{1}{4}}-2=16-2=14\end{aligned}$
